known_differences_from_fetch_script: Unit: the 2021-2025 layer (slug atlanta_apd_ga_0) is one row per offense within an incident (270,423 rows, 259,803 distinct IncidentNumber, up to 7 rows per incident; raw_cache query). The contract keeps one row per incident and mapped offense (mapping.dedup_unit incident_offense over IncidentNumber / Report_Number), so an incident with two of the seven offenses counts in both and two NIBRS codes of one offense (two 23x larceny codes, 11A and 11B) count once; no SRS hierarchy rule is applied. 659 in-year incidents carry two or three distinct mapped offenses (e.g. 87 murder+aggravated assault, 287 larceny+motor vehicle theft; map_rows crosstab on the archive).

Unit: the 2018-2020 layer (slug atlanta_apd_ga_1) is one row per report with a single Crime_Type (72,789 rows, 72,782 distinct Report_Number; raw_cache_profile.json). Whether APD applied a hierarchy when assigning the one Crime_Type is not documented.

Victim counting: SRS/NIBRS-SRS-equivalent totals count murder and aggravated assault per victim; the feed has one row per offense with a Vic_Count field the contract cannot weight by. For NibrsUcrCode 13A, 2021-2025 rows are 2647/2495/2203/1973/2387 against Vic_Count sums 3583/3315/2790/2528/3147 and official totals 3475/3166/2688/2444/2976 (raw_cache query; evidence/official_totals.csv), so the footprint aggravated-assault count is about 0.76-0.82 of the official total. For 09A, rows 148/165/131/120/97 against Vic_Count sums 157/171/136/124/100 and official 161/171/132/126/100.

Rape 2018-2020: the 2009_2020CrimeData layer has no rape category (Crime_Type has 7 values: LARCENY-FROM VEHICLE, LARCENY-NON VEHICLE, AUTO THEFT, BURGLARY, AGG ASSAULT, ROBBERY, HOMICIDE; raw_cache_profile.json), so rape is unmapped for 2018-2020 against official totals of 245, 175 and 45.

Rape 2021-2025 (11A+11B+11C) exceeds the official totals: footprint 192/182/137/141/146 against 159/164/116/79/127 (ratios 1.21, 1.11, 1.18, 1.78, 1.15; contract funnel on the archive vs evidence/official_totals.csv). 11D fondling (853 rows) and 36B statutory rape (41 rows) are not mapped.

Murder 2018-2020: Crime_Type HOMICIDE is mapped whole. Its NIBRS_Code values are 911 (138), NULL (101), 09A (46), 903 (31), 912 (13), 904 (8), 901 (2), 902 (2), 999 (1), 2902 (1) (raw_cache query); the publisher does not define these local codes, so whether HOMICIDE includes negligent manslaughter or justifiable homicide cannot be settled from the evidence.

Old-layer categories are APD's Part I groupings, not NIBRS codes: AGG ASSAULT (local codes 1313/1314/1315/1315K/1399, 13A, NULL, one 1006), LARCENY-NON VEHICLE (includes 3 rows coded 1316 and single rows coded 105, 1203X, 2206) are mapped whole as aggravated_assault and larceny.

Dates: 2021-2025 use OccurredFromDate (occurrence); 2018-2020 use Report_Date (report), because the old layer publishes occurrence only as the text field Occur_Date (M/D/YYYY) and the runner applies one date_format to the coalesced date field (an auto parse of OccurredFromDate|Occur_Date put all 270,423 new-layer rows in 1970). By Occur_Date the old layer would hold 25,712/25,018/21,848 rows in 2018/2019/2020 against 25,723/25,063/22,003 by Report_Date.

Seam: the old layer ends at Report_Date 2020-12-31 and the new layer starts at OccurredFromDate 2021-01-01 05:00 UTC (local midnight), so offenses that occurred in 2020 and were reported in 2021 or later are in neither pull.

Time zone: OccurredFromDate is stored in UTC (dateFieldsTimeReference UTC, preferredTimeReference America/New_York in doc_164a18f5b3.json; hourly counts trough at 10 UTC); the year is taken in UTC, so offenses from 19:00-24:00 local on Dec 31 count in the next year (15-22 mapped rows per boundary, 2022-2025), and those of Dec 31 2025 after 19:00 local are outside the archive's filter.

Footprint: 3,621 in-state mapped rows fall outside the Atlanta city block groups; 3,512 of them are Zone 'Airport' (new layer, 3,113) or Zone 7 (old layer, 399), and 3,186 are in Clayton County (13063) block groups (Hartsfield-Jackson airport). The official ORI GAAPD0000 totals include these offenses, so footprint larceny and motor vehicle theft understate the agency total by up to 1,038 rows a year (2024).
notes: Two ArcGIS layers, kept as the registry lists them (same slugs, name, endpoints, portal_type, select [], where with {start}/{end}, order '', page_size 1000; the source dicts hash to the archived live/ pull names 2e97a98fb547 and d1871dfdc801). Offenses: new layer by NibrsUcrCode (09A murder; 11A/11B/11C rape; 120 robbery; 13A aggravated assault; 220 burglary; 23A-23H larceny; 240 motor vehicle theft); 09B, 09C, 11D, 13B and 13C are not mapped (09B and 09C do not occur in the pull). Old layer by Crime_Type (HOMICIDE murder, ROBBERY, AGG ASSAULT, BURGLARY, LARCENY-FROM VEHICLE and LARCENY-NON VEHICLE larceny, AUTO THEFT motor vehicle theft); it has no rape category. Every mapped value occurs in the pull (raw_cache_profile.json). count_unit offense: mapping.dedup_unit incident_offense over id_fields IncidentNumber|Report_Number keeps one row per incident and mapped offense (new layer) and one per report and mapped offense (old layer); all mapped offenses of a multi-offense incident are kept, and two NIBRS codes of one offense in an incident count once. This differs from the registry's 'incident': deduplicating on IncidentNumber keeps the first row in pull order (OBJECTID order) with no hierarchy, which dropped the murder in 38 of 87 murder+aggravated-assault incidents and gave 965 murders instead of 1,004 for 2018-2025 (same runner on the archive). Dedupe removes 70 rows (185,274 to 185,204): 63 larceny incidents with two 23x codes, 4 rape incidents with 11A+11B or 11A+11C, and 4 same-code duplicate rows (aggravated assault 2, burglary 1, motor vehicle theft 1). Dates: OccurredFromDate (occurrence, epoch ms, UTC) for 2021-2025, Report_Date (report date, stored at UTC midnight) for 2018-2020, coalesced as OccurredFromDate|Report_Date with epoch_ms. Coordinates: the feature geometry (__arcgis_latitude/__arcgis_longitude, returned in WGS84) with the Latitude/Longitude attributes as fallback; the two are identical on every row of both layers. Points carry 2-9 decimals and repeat at address points (62,496 distinct points for 270,423 new-layer rows); the publisher states no rounding or offset. No (0,0) or missing points; 104 new-layer rows lie outside an Atlanta bounding box (lat 33.6-33.9, lon -84.6 to -84.28), down to Florida and New Jersey. Scope: Atlanta city (13:municipal:place:1304000), the only scope candidate; state 13. The layer descriptions are empty and the hub page states no redactions or exclusions; the registry's redactions field is empty. Funnel on the archive with this contract: raw 343,212; mapped 188,896; dated 188,896; in years 188,896; located 188,896; in state 188,895; in footprint 185,274; deduplicated 185,204. Official totals for 2019 and 2020 sit well below the feed for every property offense (e.g. 2020 larceny 4,349 against 13,188) and look partial; that is a property of the totals, not the mapping.
